result.rationale: The formula is applied correctly (0.65 x 33.3 + 0.35 x 74.29 = 47.7) and Watch is defensible on the evidence as recorded. However, the band placement rests almost entirely on a single uncorroborated two-sentence article: the news component supplies 26.0 of the 47.7 points, and without it the payment score of 21.7 alone would fall in the Healthy band. Separately, the payment input captures only the 25 DPD and is blind to the fact that open exposure of EUR 1,549,800 exceeds the EUR 1,450,000 credit limit, on a file with only one settled invoice. The payment snapshot also predates the wage-delay report by three weeks, so the 33.3 payment score likely understates current condition and the underwriter should refresh it before the score goes out.

concerns.issue: This single article contributes 26.0 of the 47.7 total score - more than half. Without it the payment score of 21.7 would place the buyer in the Healthy band, so the entire Watch classification turns on it. The underlying body is only two sentences from one publication (Business Dispatch) with no corroborating source, yet carries severity 5. The entity match is direct (not via parent) and the Birmingham location is consistent, so the signal is plausible, but a band placement resting wholly on an uncorroborated stub should be confirmed against a second source.

The payment review records total open exposure of EUR 1,549,800 against an active credit limit of EUR 1,450,000 - an overage of roughly EUR 99,800. The payment score reads only DPD (25 days) and is structurally blind to this limit breach, so the 33.3 raw payment score does not reflect that the buyer is already over its approved line.

Payment evidence is dated 2026-08-31 while the news event is dated 2026-09-20 - the payment snapshot predates the reported distress by roughly three weeks. Of the total exposure, only EUR 329,100 was past due at that date, with EUR 1,220,700 recorded as not yet due. If any of that pipeline has since fallen due, the 25 DPD input and the resulting payment score are understated. The payment position should be refreshed before the verdict is issued.

The review flags trend as 'insufficient_history': only one settled invoice exists (paid on time), so no payment trend can be established. The payment component of the score therefore carries lower evidential weight than a 33.3 raw figure implies, in either direction.
